q: Biodiversity comes from two words; Bio means life and diversity means _____.
e: Biodiversity comes from two words; Bio means life and diversity means variability. So we write variability. Leave multiplicity and abundance out.

q: The term 'Biodiversity' was coined by Walter G. Rosen in _____.
e: The term 'Biodiversity' was coined by Walter G. Rosen in 1985. 1985 is the word, not 1995 or 1975.

q: The term 'biodiversity' was popularized by Edward O. Wilson who is now known as 'Father of _____.
e: The term 'biodiversity' was popularized by Edward O. Wilson who is now known as 'Father of biodiversity. The blank is biodiversity. Not ecology or conservation.

q: Thus, biodiversity can be defined as the totality of genes, species and _____ of a region.
e: Thus, biodiversity can be defined as the totality of genes, species and ecosystem of a region. The blank is ecosystem. Not populations or communities.

q: This is usually taken to include diversity at _____ levels.
e: This is usually taken to include diversity at three levels. The blank is three. Not four or five.

q: The diversity of ecological complexity includes variations in ecological niches, trophic structure, food-webs and _____ etc.
e: The diversity of ecological complexity includes variations in ecological niches, trophic structure, food-webs and nutrient cycling etc. Nutrient cycling is the word, not energy flow or water cycle.

q: The ecosystems also show variations with respect to physical parameters like moisture, temperature, altitude, _____ etc.
e: The ecosystems also show variations with respect to physical parameters like moisture, temperature, altitude, precipitation etc. The blank is precipitation. Not salinity or wind speed.

q: Species diversity is defined as the number of species and _____ of each species that lives in a particular location.
e: Species diversity is defined as the number of species and abundance of each species that lives in a particular location. Abundance is the word, not richness or evenness.

q: The number of species in a community is known as species _____.
e: The number of species in a community is known as species richness. So we write richness. Leave evenness and diversity out.

q: Species diversity not only considers richness, but also includes a measure of the _____ of the abundance of the different species.
e: Species diversity not only considers richness, but also includes a measure of the evenness of the abundance of the different species. The blank is evenness. Not variability or density.

q: Coral reefs have a very high biodiversity; such an ecosystem offers many different _____, which are exploited by different species.
e: Coral reefs have a very high biodiversity; such an ecosystem offers many different ecological niches, which are exploited by different species. So we write ecological niches. Leave trophic levels and genetic pools out.

q: Species diversity is considered important because ecosystems with high species diversity tend to be more _____ than ones with limited diversity.
e: Species diversity is considered important because ecosystems with high species diversity tend to be more stable than ones with limited diversity. The blank is stable. Not productive or complex.

q: Genetic diversity refers to the variety of genetic information contained in all of the individual plants, animals, fungi and _____.
e: Genetic diversity refers to the variety of genetic information contained in all of the individual plants, animals, fungi and microorganisms. Microorganisms is the word, not algae or viruses.

q: The genetic differences between populations of the same species exist because populations may be adapted slightly differences in different parts of their _____.
e: The genetic differences between populations of the same species exist because populations may be adapted slightly differences in different parts of their ranges. So we write ranges. Leave habitats and niches out.

q: This diversity is important in providing populations with the ability to adapt to changes in biotic and abiotic factors, such as competition with other species, evading new predators, resisting new strains of _____.
e: This diversity is important in providing populations with the ability to adapt to changes in biotic and abiotic factors, such as competition with other species, evading new predators, resisting new strains of disease. The blank is disease. Not parasites or climate.

q: Biodiversity is very important for the well-being of our planet, human health, food security, economy and _____.
e: Biodiversity is very important for the well-being of our planet, human health, food security, economy and livelihoods. Livelihoods is the word, not technology or infrastructure.

q: Rich biodiversity allows large-scale ecosystems to function and _____.
e: Rich biodiversity allows large-scale ecosystems to function and self-regulate. The blank is self-regulate. Not self-replicate or self-destruct.

q: A healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity will increase ecosystem productivity; each species in an ecosystem has a specific _____ which is a role to play.
e: A healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity will increase ecosystem productivity; each species in an ecosystem has a specific niche which is a role to play. So we write niche. Leave habitat and population out.

q: Which of the following is a function of a healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity?
e: The answer is protect fresh water resources. Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity will increase ecosystem productivity. Not increase soil erosion or decrease climate stability.

q: Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity aid in breaking down _____.
e: Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity aid in breaking down pollutants. So we write pollutants. Leave nutrients and oxygen out.

q: Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity contribute to climate _____.
e: Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity contribute to climate stability. So we write stability. Leave change and warming out.

q: Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity speed recovery from _____.
e: Healthy ecosystem and rich biodiversity speed recovery from natural disasters. The blank is natural disasters. Not diseases or pollutants.

q: If biodiversity is reduced in one area, the natural balance may be destroyed _____.
e: If biodiversity is reduced in one area, the natural balance may be destroyed elsewhere. The blank is elsewhere. Not nowhere or there.

q: Genetic diversity is the variety of _____ within a species.
e: Genetic diversity is the variety of genes within a species. The blank is genes. Not cells or ecosystems.

q: The genetic diversity that exists between varieties of cultivated plants and domesticated animals is obvious, but similar genetic diversity exists in natural _____.
e: The genetic diversity that exists between varieties of cultivated plants and domesticated animals is obvious, but similar genetic diversity exists in natural populations. So we write populations. Leave species and communities out.

q: Myanmar is the largest country in mainland Southeast Asia with a land area of _____.
e: Myanmar is the largest country in mainland Southeast Asia with a land area of 676,577 km². 676,577 km² is the word, not 576,677 km² or 766,577 km².

q: Myanmar has a large latitudinal range of _____ km.
e: Myanmar has a large latitudinal range of 2,100 km. So we write 2,100. Leave 1,200 and 3,100 out.

q: The total area of forest in Myanmar is 290,410 km² which is _____ of the total land area.
e: The total area of forest in Myanmar is 290,410 km² which is 43% of the total land area. So we write 43%. Leave 33% and 53% out.

q: According to Table 6.1, which forest type covers the highest percentage of forest areas in Myanmar?
e: The answer is Mixed Deciduous Forest. Dry Forest makes up 10% of Forest Areas in Myanmar. Not Tropical Evergreen Forest or Hill and Temperate Evergreen Forest.

q: What percentage of forest areas in Myanmar is covered by Hill and Temperate Evergreen Forest?
e: The answer is 25%. Tropical Evergreen Forest makes up 16% of Forest Areas in Myanmar. Not 38% or 16%.

q: Tropical Evergreen Forest covers _____ % of forest areas in Myanmar.
e: Tropical Evergreen Forest covers 16% % of forest areas in Myanmar. The blank is 16%. Not 10% or 5%.

q: Dry forest occurs where rainfall is usually less than _____ mm a year and support xerophytic types of vegetation.
e: Dry forest occurs where rainfall is usually less than 400 mm a year and support xerophytic types of vegetation. So we write 400. Leave 600 and 200 out.

q: Deciduous Dipterocarp (Indaing) Forest covers _____ % of forest areas in Myanmar.
e: Deciduous Dipterocarp (Indaing) Forest covers 5% % of forest areas in Myanmar. 5% is the word, not 10% or 4%.

q: Which organization publishes the Red Data Book, which includes the list of endangered species of plants and animals?
e: The answer is IUCN. The International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) publishes the Red Data Book, which includes the list of endangered species of plants and animals. Not WHO or WWF.

q: The red data symbolizes the warning signal for those species, which are endangered and if not protected are likely to become _____ in near future.
e: The red data symbolizes the warning signal for those species, which are endangered and if not protected are likely to become extinct in near future. The blank is extinct. Not endemic or invasive.

q: About _____ mammal species are recorded in Myanmar.
e: About 250 mammal species are recorded in Myanmar. The blank is 250. Not 350 or 150.

q: More than _____ birds are recorded in Myanmar.
e: More than 1,000 birds are recorded in Myanmar. The blank is 1,000. Not 500 or 700.

q: Among the recorded species in Myanmar, _____ species of mammals are globally threatened.
e: Among the recorded species in Myanmar, 39 species of mammals are globally threatened. So we write 39. Leave 21 and 45 out.

q: How many species of birds are globally threatened in Myanmar?
e: The answer is 45. Among the recorded species in Myanmar, 39 species of mammals are globally threatened. Not 38 or 21.

q: How many species of plants are globally threatened in Myanmar?
e: The answer is 38. Among the recorded species in Myanmar, 39 species of mammals are globally threatened. Not 21 or 45.

q: What is the Myanmar Name for the endangered plant species Dipterocarpus alatus?
e: The answer is Kanyin. Scientific Name: Dipterocarpus alatus, Common Name: Gurjum tree, IUCN Status: Endangered. Not Mahogany or Kyauk Htinn shuu.

q: What is the IUCN Status of the Black Orchid (Paphiopedilum wardii) in Myanmar?
e: The answer is Critically Endangered. Scientific Name: Paphiopedilum wardii, Common Name: Black Orchid, IUCN Status: Critically Endangered. Not Endangered or Vulnerable.

q: What is the Myanmar Name for the endangered plant species Cephalotaxus mannii?
e: The answer is Kyauk Htinn shuu. CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Flora and Fauna. Not Thit-khwa net or Taung Zalat Ni.

q: The Asian Elephant (Elephas maximus) has an IUCN Status of _____.
e: The Asian Elephant (Elephas maximus) has an IUCN Status of endangered. Endangered is the word, not Critically Endangered or vulnerable.

q: What is the Myanmar Name for the Irrawaddy Dolphin (Orcaella brevirostris)?
e: The answer is Linpai. Orcaella brevirostris is commonly known as the Irrawaddy Dolphin and its IUCN Status is Endangered. Not Sin or Daun.

q: The Burmese Star Tortoise (Geochelone platynota) has an IUCN Status of _____.
e: The Burmese Star Tortoise (Geochelone platynota) has an IUCN Status of Critically Endangered. So we write Critically Endangered. Leave endangered and extinct out.

q: What is the common name for the endangered vertebrate species Rucervus eldii thamin?
e: The answer is Eld's Deer. Scientific Name: Rucervus eldii thamin, Common Name: Eld's Deer, Myanmar Name: Shwe Thamin. Not Asian Elephant or Green Peafowl.

q: What is the Myanmar Name for the Green Peafowl (Pavo muticus)?
e: The answer is Daun. Scientific Name: Pavo muticus, Common Name: Green Peafowl, Myanmar Name: Daun. Not Shwe Thamin or Kyelait.

q: Forests help regulates the seasonal flow of water downstream and recharge sources of _____.
e: Forests help regulates the seasonal flow of water downstream and recharge sources of groundwater. The blank is groundwater. Not surface water or rainwater.

q: By impeding the loss of soils, forests help to maintain the functioning of _____ infrastructure.
e: By impeding the loss of soils, forests help to maintain the functioning of dam and reservoir infrastructure. The blank is dam and reservoir. Not agricultural or transportation.

q: More than 3 billion people depend on marine and coastal biodiversity, while more than _____ billion people rely on forests for their livelihoods.
e: More than 3 billion people depend on marine and coastal biodiversity, while more than 1.6 billion people rely on forests for their livelihoods. So we write 1.6. Leave 2.6 and 3.6 out.

q: The loss of biodiversity affects the lives of more than _____ billion people living in dry lands.
e: The loss of biodiversity affects the lives of more than 1 billion people living in dry lands. The blank is 1. Not 3 or 2.

q: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the five major threats to biodiversity?
e: The answer is captive breeding. There are five major threats to biodiversity. Not habitat loss or climate change.

q: The clearing of land for agriculture, housing, transport, leisure facilities and industry removes vegetation, leading to habitat _____.
e: The clearing of land for agriculture, housing, transport, leisure facilities and industry removes vegetation, leading to habitat fragmentation. Fragmentation is the word, not restoration or expansion.

q: Physically larger species and those living at lower latitudes or in forests or oceans are more sensitive to reduction in habitat _____.
e: Physically larger species and those living at lower latitudes or in forests or oceans are more sensitive to reduction in habitat area. The blank is area. Not quality or connectivity.

q: Which of the following is a major reason for habitat destruction mentioned in the text?
e: The answer is dam construction. Shifting cultivation in upland areas and gold mining are major reasons for habitat destruction in Myanmar. Not seed banking or captive breeding.

q: Factors such as the replacement of local landraces with modern varieties and overgrazing are major threats to the _____ of Myanmar.
e: Factors such as the replacement of local landraces with modern varieties and overgrazing are major threats to the agrobiodiversity of Myanmar. The blank is agrobiodiversity. Not marine biodiversity or ex situ conservation.

q: Pollution is caused by uncontrolled pesticide and herbicide uses, various factory wastes, different kinds of rubbish, human sewage, radioactive materials and _____.
e: Pollution is caused by uncontrolled pesticide and herbicide uses, various factory wastes, different kinds of rubbish, human sewage, radioactive materials and industrial wastes. Industrial wastes is the word, not organic fertilizers or compost.

q: Invasive alien species (IAS) can be introduced unintentionally by tourists or through the transport of cargo or movement of pets, plant parts and _____.
e: Invasive alien species (IAS) can be introduced unintentionally by tourists or through the transport of cargo or movement of pets, plant parts and seeds. So we write seeds. Leave water and soil out.

q: Some invasive alien species may be intentionally imported for use in research, manufacture of medicine or ornamental and _____ uses.
e: Some invasive alien species may be intentionally imported for use in research, manufacture of medicine or ornamental and industrial uses. The blank is industrial. Not agricultural or medical.

q: Genetic pollution indicates the loss of identity of wild plant species as a result of transfer of genes from _____.
e: Genetic pollution indicates the loss of identity of wild plant species as a result of transfer of genes from crop plants. The blank is crop plants. Not wild animals or invasive species.

q: Gene flow is expected to have its greatest effect on weed species that are closely related to crop plants taxonomically, ecologically and in their reproductive _____.
e: Gene flow is expected to have its greatest effect on weed species that are closely related to crop plants taxonomically, ecologically and in their reproductive biology. The blank is biology. Not isolation or barriers.

q: The term 'genetic pollution' is usually associated with the gene flow from a genetically engineered organism to a _____ organism.
e: The term 'genetic pollution' is usually associated with the gene flow from a genetically engineered organism to a non-GE organism. Non-GE is the word, not transgenic or modified.

q: Overexploitation, also called overharvesting, can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to _____.
e: Overexploitation, also called overharvesting, can lead to the destruction of the resource, as it will be unable to replenish. Replenish is the word, not adapt or evolve.

q: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than that the species can replenish its population _____.
e: Overfishing is the removal of a species of fish from a body of water at a rate greater than that the species can replenish its population naturally. So we write naturally. Leave artificially and rapidly out.

q: Overlogging is a form of overexploitation caused by legal or illegal logging activities that lead to unsustainable or irrecoverable deforestation and permanent habitat destruction for forest _____.
e: Overlogging is a form of overexploitation caused by legal or illegal logging activities that lead to unsustainable or irrecoverable deforestation and permanent habitat destruction for forest wildlife. So we write wildlife. Leave soils and water out.

q: Overhunting threatens _____ of endangered vertebrates, as well as other groups.
e: Overhunting threatens one-third of endangered vertebrates, as well as other groups. The blank is one-third. Not one-half or two-thirds.

q: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at $_____ billion per year.
e: Excluding edible fish, the illegal trade in wildlife is valued at $10 billion per year. So we write 10. Leave 20 and 5 out.

q: Bushmeat provides increased opportunity for transmission of several zoonotic viruses from animal hosts to humans, such as Ebola virus and _____.
e: Bushmeat provides increased opportunity for transmission of several zoonotic viruses from animal hosts to humans, such as Ebola virus and HIV. HIV is the word, not malaria or dengue.

q: Climate change alters the climate patterns and ecosystems in which species have evolved and on which they _____.
e: Climate change alters the climate patterns and ecosystems in which species have evolved and on which they depend. Depend is the word, not feed or prey.

q: Rising ocean temperatures and diminishing Arctic sea ice affects marine biodiversity and can shift _____ zones.
e: Rising ocean temperatures and diminishing Arctic sea ice affects marine biodiversity and can shift vegetation zones. Vegetation is the word, not trophic or precipitation.

q: An increase in the world's population will cause additional strains on resources, leading to more deforestation, decreased biodiversity, and spikes in pollution and _____.
e: An increase in the world's population will cause additional strains on resources, leading to more deforestation, decreased biodiversity, and spikes in pollution and emissions. Emissions is the word, not conservation or recycling.

q: Wildlife trade refers to the commerce of products that are derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled _____.
e: Wildlife trade refers to the commerce of products that are derived from non-domesticated animals or plants usually extracted from their natural environment or raised under controlled conditions. Conditions is the word, not habitats or reserves.

q: Recent overexploitation of wildlife for trade has affected countless species driven by high demand from expanding illegal wildlife markets in _____ countries.
e: Recent overexploitation of wildlife for trade has affected countless species driven by high demand from expanding illegal wildlife markets in neighboring countries. So we write neighboring. Leave western and developed out.

q: In wildlife smuggling, much of demand for rhinoceros' horns, tiger bones, and other animal products arises out of the practice of traditional _____ medicine.
e: In wildlife smuggling, much of demand for rhinoceros' horns, tiger bones, and other animal products arises out of the practice of traditional chinese medicine. Chinese is the word, not ayurvedic or western.

q: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as _____% of all illegal wildlife trade.
e: The most trafficked animal in the world is the pangolin, accounting for as much as 20%% of all illegal wildlife trade. So we write 20%. Leave 10% and 50% out.

q: In the last decade, more than one million pangolins were poached and killed for their _____.
e: In the last decade, more than one million pangolins were poached and killed for their scales. The blank is scales. Not meat or bones.

q: Wildlife smuggling may cause the introduction of invasive and harmful species into an ecosystem, which can endanger indigenous wildlife by putting a strain on the environment's resources through interspecific _____.
e: Wildlife smuggling may cause the introduction of invasive and harmful species into an ecosystem, which can endanger indigenous wildlife by putting a strain on the environment's resources through interspecific competition. Competition is the word, not cooperation or symbiosis.

q: Outbreaks of zoonotic diseases including COVID-19, H5N1 avian flu, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and monkeypox have been traced to live wildlife _____.
e: Outbreaks of zoonotic diseases including COVID-19, H5N1 avian flu, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and monkeypox have been traced to live wildlife markets. So we write markets. Leave farms and reserves out.

q: CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Flora and _____.
e: CITES stands for the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Flora and fauna. So we write fauna. Leave fungi and fish out.

q: The Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law was enacted in Myanmar in the year _____.
e: The Conservation of Biodiversity and Protected Areas Law was enacted in Myanmar in the year 2018. 2018 is the word, not 2015 or 2020.

q: Certain places in the world where wildlife trade is particularly threatening or where targeted action would be particularly worthwhile are called 'wildlife trade _____.
e: Certain places in the world where wildlife trade is particularly threatening or where targeted action would be particularly worthwhile are called 'wildlife trade hotspots. So we write hotspots. Leave zones and centers out.

q: Excessive use of fertilizers and industrial and domestic forms of _____ is one of the five major threats to biodiversity.
e: Excessive use of fertilizers and industrial and domestic forms of pollution is one of the five major threats to biodiversity. So we write pollution. Leave waste and chemicals out.

q: The effects of invasive alien species on native species and especially _____ is a major threat to biodiversity.
e: The effects of invasive alien species on native species and especially endemics is a major threat to biodiversity. Endemics is the word, not exotics or migratories.

q: Conservation means keeping and protecting a living and changing _____.
e: Conservation means keeping and protecting a living and changing environment. Environment is the word, not species or population.

q: Which of the following is a Narrowly Utilitarian reason to conserve biodiversity?
a: useful human products like food and drugs
e: The answer is providing oxygen. Narrowly Utilitarian reason for conservation involves useful human products like food, fibres, drugs and medicines obtained from biodiversity. Not intrinsic value of species or useful human products like food and drugs.

q: Biodiversity provides ecosystem services like providing oxygen, pollinating crops and controlling floods, which is a _____ Utilitarian reason for conservation.
e: Biodiversity provides ecosystem services like providing oxygen, pollinating crops and controlling floods, which is a broadly Utilitarian reason for conservation. Broadly is the word, not narrowly or ethical.

q: Every living species has an intrinsic value, though it may not have direct economic value and every species has the right to live; this is an _____ Utilitarian reason.
e: Every living species has an intrinsic value, though it may not have direct economic value and every species has the right to live; this is an ethical Utilitarian reason. So we write ethical. Leave economic and broadly out.

q: In situ methods are the ways of conservation of species which take place in the _____ habitat of the organism.
e: In situ methods are the ways of conservation of species which take place in the natural habitat of the organism. The blank is natural. Not artificial or captivity.

q: Nature reserves such as wildlife sanctuary, national park and biosphere reserve help endangered species by maintaining their habitat and _____ diversity.
e: Nature reserves such as wildlife sanctuary, national park and biosphere reserve help endangered species by maintaining their habitat and genetic diversity. So we write genetic. Leave species and ecosystem out.

q: Active management of nature reserves involves continuous monitoring, maintenance of effective boundaries, measures to facilitate the successful completion of life cycles and restocking and _____ of once-common species.
e: Active management of nature reserves involves continuous monitoring, maintenance of effective boundaries, measures to facilitate the successful completion of life cycles and restocking and reintroducing of once-common species. Reintroducing is the word, not culling or hunting.

q: Ex situ methods are the ways to conserve animals and plants _____ their natural habitats.
e: Ex situ methods are the ways to conserve animals and plants outside their natural habitats. Outside is the word, not within or near.

q: In captive breeding programmes, individuals of an endangered species are bred in zoos and parks in an attempt to save the species from _____.
e: In captive breeding programmes, individuals of an endangered species are bred in zoos and parks in an attempt to save the species from extinction. Extinction is the word, not migration or competition.

q: Which of the following is a technique used in captive breeding programmes?
e: The answer is Artificial insemination. Artificial insemination and embryo transfer to a surrogate mother are techniques used in captive breeding programmes. Not habitat fragmentation or overharvesting.

q: Cryogenics in captive breeding involves freezing eggs, sperm cells and embryos for future use, while keeping a pedigree helps prevent from _____.
e: Cryogenics in captive breeding involves freezing eggs, sperm cells and embryos for future use, while keeping a pedigree helps prevent from inbreeding. Inbreeding is the word, not outbreeding or mutation.

q: It has been estimated that _____% of the world's flowering plant species could disappear within the next 50 years.
e: It has been estimated that 25%% of the world's flowering plant species could disappear within the next 50 years. 25% is the word, not 50% or 10%.

q: Seeds in a seed bank are kept in cold, dark conditions in which the metabolism of the seed slows down so the seed is prevented from _____.
e: Seeds in a seed bank are kept in cold, dark conditions in which the metabolism of the seed slows down so the seed is prevented from germinating. So we write germinating. Leave drying and rotting out.

q: Seeds in a seed bank are stored in a temperature of _____ and in dark conditions.
e: Seeds in a seed bank are stored in a temperature of -14°C and in dark conditions. The blank is -14°C. Not -4°C or -24°C.

q: Saved and viable seeds in seed banks contain a treasure trove of useful genes that breeders can use for developing improved varieties of our major _____ crops.
e: Saved and viable seeds in seed banks contain a treasure trove of useful genes that breeders can use for developing improved varieties of our major food crops. So we write food. Leave ornamental and timber out.

q: About _____ plant species are grown in private gardens, arboretums and botanical gardens all over the world.
e: About 80,000 plant species are grown in private gardens, arboretums and botanical gardens all over the world. The blank is 80,000. Not 40,000 or 60,000.

q: Botanical gardens not only serve as taxonomic and systematic research centers but they play an important role as valuable sources of plant _____.
e: Botanical gardens not only serve as taxonomic and systematic research centers but they play an important role as valuable sources of plant ecology. Ecology is the word, not anatomy or physiology.

q: In Myanmar, _____ protected areas have been established under various categories.
e: In Myanmar, 42 protected areas have been established under various categories. 42 is the word, not 52 or 32.

q: Which protected area category is held for the protection of their features for 'scientific study, research, education, and the benefit of the country'?
e: The answer is Scientific reserve. A scientific reserve is held for the protection of their features for scientific study, research, education, and the benefit of the country. Not National park or Wildlife sanctuary.

q: A _____ is an area set aside by a national government for the preservation of the natural environment where no settlement or resource harvesting is allowed.
e: A National park is an area set aside by a national government for the preservation of the natural environment where no settlement or resource harvesting is allowed. The blank is National park. Not Community forest or Nature reserve.

q: Lampi Island Marine National Park is an example of a _____ national park.
e: Lampi Island Marine National Park is an example of a marine national park. Marine is the word, not terrestrial or scientific.

q: A _____ is a protected area of importance for flora, fauna, or features of geological or other special interest, reserved for conservation and study, e.g., Popa Mountain Park.
e: A Nature reserve is a protected area of importance for flora, fauna, or features of geological or other special interest, reserved for conservation and study,, Popa Mountain Park. Nature reserve is the word, not Wildlife sanctuary or Community forest.

q: In a wildlife sanctuary, the capturing, killing and _____ of animals is strictly prohibited.
e: In a wildlife sanctuary, the capturing, killing and poaching of animals is strictly prohibited. Poaching is the word, not feeding or breeding.

q: Hlawga Park and Chatthin Wildlife Sanctuary are examples of _____ in Myanmar.
e: Hlawga Park and Chatthin Wildlife Sanctuary are examples of Wildlife sanctuaries in Myanmar. So we write Wildlife sanctuaries. Leave National parks and Marine parks out.

q: In the early _____, the Government of Myanmar introduced Community forest (CF) as a way to protect endangered forest resources.
e: In the early 1990s, the Government of Myanmar introduced Community forest (CF) as a way to protect endangered forest resources. 1990s is the word, not 2000s or 1980s.

q: Community forest means all sustainable forest management and utilization activities, in which the local _____ itself is involved.
e: Community forest means all sustainable forest management and utilization activities, in which the local community itself is involved. So we write community. Leave government and military out.
